text:
sam: Heads up — saw a regression in paged-attn throughput during the night load test. Token/sec down ~15% for 8k sequences when KV pager churned. Logs point at kernel fallback churn and allocator pressure.

maria: Can you paste the perf slice and the relevant logs?

sam: Pasting a short slice from the profiler + logs: 
```
2026-03-18T02:14:03Z perf: model=paged-attn seq=8192 batch=4 tokens/sec=5200 (baseline 6150)
attn_kernel: chosen=flash_v2 variant=flash_v2_opt fallback=naive after 7ms (kv_miss=0.28)
KV_PAGER: evict_count=1247 page_in=930 page_out=905 frag_percent=42
ALLOC: slab_alloc_fail=0x3, fallback_to_heap=1, alloc_requests=12043
block_table: size=131072 entries=98765 rehashes=4 last_rehash=00:01:22
```
Also saw `kv_pager: handoff=true -> handoff=false` flips where a page handoff completed then immediate eviction pulled it out.

jordan: That block_table growth + high frag% screams allocation fragmentation. Which allocator mode did you run? hybrid or slab-only?

sam: hybrid with slab warmup and compact_on_eviction=true. We intentionally keep bucket_size=64 to favor locality.

kai: Two quick hypotheses: 1) heavy KV miss rate causes flash_v2 to fall back to the naive kernel more often because the KV cache cold-start inflates latency; 2) allocator fragmentation leads to page table rehashing which stalls the pager threads and blocks batching.

kai: Try this quick experiment locally: toggle compact_on_eviction=false and lower bucket_size to 32, then run bench: `./bench/paged_attn --seq 8192 --batch 4 --iters 200`

sam: Ran that. Short results: baseline (prod config) tokens/sec 6150; repro config (compact=false, bucket=32) tokens/sec 5980; minimal improvement but p95 latency dropped from 42ms -> 35ms on the paged path.

diego: I reproduced a race I think. In pager_handoff() we do: 
```c
// simplified\atomic_store(&handoff_inflight, true);
copy_page_to_new_owner();
atomic_store(&handoff_inflight, false);
// eviction thread checks handoff_inflight and may evict concurrently
```
If eviction sees handoff_inflight false between copy and commit, it can evict the page which causes the kernel to see a KV miss immediately after a handoff — churn. Need a commit barrier or flip sequence.

maria: Nice catch. Adding a commit sequence number to the page metadata would let eviction check `page.seq == expected_seq` instead of a single handoff flag. Small change but low-risk.

kai: Also check kernel selection thresholds: if flash_v2 has a fragility threshold around kv_miss_rate > 0.2 it falls back. We should expose a transient hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during short KV storms. Eg: require miss_rate > 0.25 for 3 consecutive eval windows (200ms windows).

sam: Agreed. Quick patch matrix: (A) add seq commit to page handoff, (B) add hysteresis to kernel chooser, (C) try compact_on_eviction=false in a canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for paged-attn hostgroup `pg-attn-canary-2` with config overrides {compact_on_eviction:false, bucket_size:32, kernel_hysteresis:3}.

maria: I'll instrument additional histograms around `pager_wait_ms` and `kernel_select_count` — want per-route traces for the next 4 hours.

jordan: If A fixes the race we should see page_in/page_out balance normalize and block_table rehashes drop. Watch `block_table.rehashes` and `slab_frag_percent`.

sam: Running an isolated load now against the canary: 
```
# warmup run
./bench/paged_attn --seq 8192 --batch 4 --iters 120 --target pg-attn-canary-2
# sample output
tokens/sec=6100 p95=34ms kernel: flash_v2 chosen=95% fallback=5% kv_miss=0.12 frag=24%
```

diego: That's promising — fallback went from ~30% to 5% in your sample. If stable, that matches the hysteresis + reduced frag hypothesis.

maria: Also saw fewer `slab_alloc_fail` entries in logs on the canary. Will let traces run.

kai: Assuming stable for 2h, propose we roll the config to the next 20% of capacity. Also queue small patch for handoff->seq commit; keep it small and feature-flagged.

sam: I'll open an RFC + cherry-pick: `rfc/2026-03-paged-kv-handoff-seq.md` and a tiny runtime toggle `pager.handoff_seq_enabled`.

maria: Good. If anyone has additional microbench tweaks for batching heuristics (batch thresholds, early flush windows) throw them in the RFC.

jordan: One more thought — check whether embedding/encoder workloads with heavier beam sizes are more sensitive. Might need model-specific kernel profiles.

sam: Noted. For now monitoring looks green on the canary after 25m: tokens/sec ~6070 steady, kernel fallback ~6%, slab_frag down to 26%. Will update RFC and follow up. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: monitor-bot: alert suppressed for pg-attn-canary-2 (auto-suppress)

maria: Thanks everyone — great triage. We'll keep this thread open for the RFC + rollout notes.
